title: Under an integral ring map, a maximal ideal contracts to a maximal ideal
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] (every element of $S$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi(R)$). If $\mathfrak n\subset S$ is a maximal ideal, then $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is a maximal ideal of $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OI (lemma-going-up-maximal-on-top, line 27335), applied to the integral map $R\to S$, which has the going-up property by Lemma Tag 00GU (lemma-integral-going-up, line 7853)

mathlib_searches.query: the contraction of a maximal ideal along an integral ring homomorphism is maximal
If S is integral over R and I is a maximal ideal of S, then its preimage in R is a maximal ideal
